text:
maria: Heads-up — multiple GPU nodes in eu-central failing image pulls after the config push, looks DNS-related. pods stuck in ImagePullBackOff :confused:
sam: Seen similar earlier in apac, did you get the hostnames? any NXDOMAIN or timeouts in kubelet logs?
maria: Logs show: 
```
kubelet: lookup registry.internal: no such host
containerd: dial tcp: lookup registry.internal on 10.0.0.2:53: read udp 10.0.0.10:54823->10.0.0.2:53: i/o timeout
```
adele: 10.0.0.2 is the node-local-dns we deployed. Are nodes still pointed at the cluster DNS or leaking to egress?
liam: Quick note: we rolled a NAT egress change earlier to consolidate IGW rules. Could have changed source IP and triggered our ISP split-horizon upstream to send public answers instead of internal ones.
maria: That matches — these images should resolve to internal registry VIPs (10.42.x.x) but hosts got public A records which don't exist internally. Some lookups get NXDOMAIN, others return wrong public IP.
sam: Can you paste a sample resolv.conf from a failing node?
maria: On a failing node: 
```
search svc.cluster.local cluster.local
nameserver 10.0.0.2
options ndots:5 single-request-reopen
```
adele: ndots:5 is fine. But node-local-dns forwards to our egress were previously pinned to 10.0.0.5 (private resolvers). If the NAT change rewrote source to a different subnets IP, upstream may be using ACL-based split-horizon.
infra-bot: Incident created: #INC-4492 — cluster DNS mismatches causing image-pull failures (severity: medium)
liam: I kicked off tcpdump on node -> saw queries to 10.0.0.2 then 10.0.0.2 forwarding to 198.51.100.10:53 (our ISP resolver). They answered with public records.
sam: So we have two issues: node-local-resolver forwarding externally *and* TTL caching on nodes returning stale answers for the internal registry after failover. How widespread?
maria: ~4 nodes in the eu-central GPU pool, 12 pods affected. Non-GPU nodes in same AZ unaffected (different egress path).
adele: Repro: from a failing node: `dig registry.internal @10.0.0.2 +short` returns public IP; `dig registry.internal @10.0.0.5 +short` returns internal VIP.
liam: Quick mitigation: force node-local-dns to prefer internal upstreams by updating configmap `node-local-dns` stubDomains -> point `registry.internal` to 10.0.0.5. Rolling this now to affected nodes.
sam: Also change iptables SNAT to preserve original source for DNS? That might be larger blast. For now configmap override + flush DNS caches should fix.
maria: Flushed systemd-resolved cache on nodes and restarted `kubelet` on the 4 bad nodes. Pulls resumed for 2 nodes, remaining 2 still failing — their node-local-dns cached the bad answers with TTL 300s.
adele: We should reduce TTL for registry.internal in upstream authoritative DNS to 60s next change window. Also add a health check in the infra console to detect when cluster resolves registry.internal to non-internal ranges.
liam: Agreed. Action items: 
- roll node-local-dns config (done)
- flush caches + restart on affected nodes (in progress)
- revert NAT egress change or patch SNAT rules (sam/infra)
- reduce TTL on internal zone (adele/dns)
- add alert for split-horizon mismatches (maria)

maria: Noting cost impact: autoscaler saw ImagePullBackOff -> created new nodes then drained old ones, we briefly doubled GPU capacity and billed additional reserved instances — ticketing cost ops.
sam: Oof. Add cost tag to incident. We'll also make rollout policy for NAT changes include a DNS smoke test.
liam: Update: after flushing caches and restarting node-local-dns on the last two nodes, image pulls recovered. rolling verification across the pool now.
adele: Postmortem thoughts: implicit dependency on egress source IP for external split-horizon is brittle. We should prefer auth internal resolvers that don't rely on source-based views, and add an explicit egress DNS policy for node-local-dns.
maria: Thanks team. I'll file postmortem and include timeline + cost delta. tagging @oncall for follow-up. :thumbsup:
